defect_observations.detail: def:p02-syllogistic-literal-closure, thm:p02-syllogistic-closure and thm:p02-syllogistic-extension are stated for an arbitrary Phi, whereas PHM 2008 v1 Lemmas 3.3-3.5 (pp.14-15) assume Phi is a set of universal formulas. The second sentence of thm:p02-syllogistic-extension ('Such a complete extension defines a one-element structure satisfying Phi') is false for non-universal Phi: thm:p02-w02c-p02-002-existential-closure (w02c-p02-002.tex lines 137-151) is a counterexample with Phi = {E(p,q)} and {p-bar}, and the annex proof (annex/p02/syllogistic-inference.tex lines 212-218) checks universal premises only. Every use in the completeness proofs applies the lemma to the universal part Phi, so no case of the source's proof is missing; the statement should carry the hypothesis 'Phi a set of universal sentences'. Read-only host for this packet.

The packet's new owned files are already input from the editable hosts (parts line 342; annex categorical-syllogistic-and-existential-import-w02-p02-002.tex line 271), so their content is on the route now. The packet's insertion plan (handbook/parts/p02.tex after line 165; handbook/annex/p02.tex after line 61) would input them a second time and duplicate the chapter and its labels; only one routing should remain.

Not counted as gaps: PHM p.7's remark that Theta |= theta is taken as a rational reconstruction of valid inference and p.8's remark that the identifications make no essential difference to the results are not restated. Both are remarks, not definitions, and lie outside the unit's Section 2 extent ('definitions needed for S and S-dagger'). Section 3, whose extent is complete, has every rule, remark, lemma, theorem and proof case on the route.
